answer: One defense is a single admission inlet: every new agent must publish a hashed identity commitment, then wait a full epoch before revealing it and transacting. Reviewers act like a prism, splitting the batch of reveals by timing, funding source and behaviour; clusters that arrive together from one funder are collapsed into one identity with one vote. An attacker wanting a thousand fakes must fund a thousand separately aged commitments and park each on an idle mesa for an epoch, so cost scales with the number of fakes while an honest agent pays once.
